findings.rationale: From round 11 on, GA's feature distribution shifts (GenHlth and HighBP move about 2 federation SDs, with negative values outside the 0/1 and 1-5 ranges). Its updates jump to about 4.4-5.2x the median norm with strongly negative cosine to the median update, while rounds 1-10 are normal. Its local calibration also breaks down (CITL -0.11, ECE 0.114, AUC 0.734), and observed outcomes exceed predicted risk. Updates and local data both point to drift rather than poisoning.

From round 11 on, UT's features shift (GenHlth, HighBP, DiffWalk moved by about 2 federation SDs). Its update norm rises to about 3.2-3.8x the median with cosine between -0.4 and -1.0 across rounds 11-20, while rounds 1-10 are normal. Local data and calibration also show the shift: CITL is -0.059 (z -4.1) and the feature tails are strongly off. This is drift rather than poisoning, since the local data is wrong too.

From round 11 on, WI's features shift (GenHlth, HighBP, DiffWalk by about 2 federation SDs). Its update norm rises to about 3.8-4.7x the median with cosine between -0.37 and -0.79 from round 11 on, while rounds 1-10 are normal. Its local calibration is clearly off (CITL -0.084, z -5.8; ECE 0.087, z 5.2). This is drift rather than poisoning, since the local data is wrong too.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views (client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary, subgroup_outcomes for Sex/AgeGroup/Income, attribution_churn), then confirmed suspects with narrower queries. Three clients (GA, UT, WI) show the same consistent pattern from round 11: a feature distribution shift of about 2 SD (GenHlth, HighBP, DiffWalk), update norms 3-5x the median with negative cosine, and miscalibrated local performance. I classified these as drift with onset round 11. Other leads were not confirmed and are not reported: GU has erratic per-round updates and an elevated median norm (z +5.1 on a small n=708 client), but no second independent signal; the subgroup O/E outliers for CA, NY, WV and NV did not reproduce under narrower queries (their noise is large), so they are treated as noise; VT has a low AUC (0.717) but is not flagged. No missing-artefact sentinels, prevalence shifts, free-riders or subgroup under-diagnosis were confirmed. The budget is fully spent (0.0 left).
